name: Ethernet
description: Local link framing and media access using MAC addresses.
uses: Connects endpoints and switches within a broadcast domain.

name: ARP
description: Resolves an IPv4 next-hop address to a link-layer address on a local network.
uses: A host discovers its gateway MAC before sending an off-link IPv4 packet.

name: IPv4
description: Connectionless packet delivery with 32-bit addressing.
uses: Carries TCP, UDP, and ICMP between routed networks.

name: IPv6
description: Connectionless packet delivery with 128-bit addressing and a fixed base header.
uses: Provides end-to-end addressing across IPv6 networks.

name: ICMP
description: Reports IPv4 control information and selected delivery errors.
uses: Echo testing and Time Exceeded messages support troubleshooting.

name: ICMPv6
description: IPv6 error reporting and control messaging.
uses: Packet Too Big and Neighbor Discovery are necessary IPv6 functions.

name: Neighbor Discovery
description: ICMPv6 messages discover neighbors and routers and test reachability.
uses: Router Advertisements tell hosts about prefixes and default routers.

name: TCP
description: Reliable ordered byte-stream transport with flow and congestion control.
uses: SSH and many HTTP connections use TCP.

name: UDP
description: Datagram transport without built-in delivery or ordering guarantees.
uses: DNS, voice, and QUIC applications can build on UDP.

name: QUIC
description: Secure multiplexed transport over UDP with independent streams.
uses: HTTP/3 uses QUIC to avoid TCP's cross-stream head-of-line blocking.

name: HTTP
description: Request-response semantics for web resources and APIs.
uses: GET retrieves a representation; status codes describe the result.

name: TLS 1.3
description: Authenticates peers and protects application data in transit.
uses: HTTPS validates a certificate and derives traffic encryption keys.

name: DNS
description: Distributed hierarchical naming and resource-record lookup.
uses: A and AAAA records identify addresses; MX records identify mail exchangers.

name: DHCPv4
description: Leases IPv4 configuration through discover, offer, request, and acknowledgement exchanges.
uses: A client obtains an address, mask, router, and DNS settings.

name: DHCPv6
description: Supplies IPv6 addresses, delegated prefixes, and configuration options.
uses: A router obtains a delegated prefix; hosts learn default routers through RA.

name: SSH
description: Encrypted remote login and authenticated channel transport.
uses: An administrator uses key authentication for a server session.

name: BGP-4
description: Policy-based routing between autonomous systems and within provider networks.
uses: Peers advertise IP prefixes and path attributes over TCP.

name: OSPFv2
description: Link-state interior routing for IPv4.
uses: Routers compute shortest paths from a shared area topology.

name: NTPv4
description: Synchronizes clocks using time servers and delay estimation.
uses: Consistent timestamps support authentication and incident analysis.

name: SNMPv3
description: Management framework supporting authenticated and protected device monitoring.
uses: A monitoring server queries interface counters with scoped credentials.

name: IPsec
description: Protects IP traffic using security associations and packet-level protocols.
uses: A site-to-site tunnel protects packets between gateways.

name: Spanning Tree
description: Prevents forwarding loops in bridged Ethernet topologies.
uses: A redundant link is blocked until a topology change needs it.
